full_judgment:
A.T.M. Afzal, J.: This appeal by the plaintiff following leave is from order dated 11 April, 1993 (Civil Order no. 1053 of 1993) passed by a Division Bench of the High Court Division summarily rejecting the revisional application of the appellant filed against order dated 4.4.93 of the Subordinate Judge, Bagerhat in Title Suit No. 1 of 1993 refusing to grant stay of further proceeding pursuant to a Government letter dated 13.3.93 addressed to the Deputy Commissioner, Bagerhat, conveying Government decision to grant lease of the 'Delbhasani Jalmahal' to defendant no. 5 for the years 1400-1402 B.S. 

 6. Mr. Md. Hannan, Learned Advocate for Respondent No. 5, argued that the report of  the Thana Nirbahi Officer dated 29.12. 92 clearly stated that the Jalmahal was not within any particular 'Gher' nor anybody had put up 'Bheri Bundh' fixing boundary for establishing a 'Gher' and that the learned Subordinate Judge having found no prima facie case in favour of the plaintiff, the prayer for stay of the Government order was rightly rejected. He stated that the order of the Government (dated 13. 3. 93) had already been acted upon by payment of rent (by respondent No. 5) for 1400 B. S. on 10.4. 93 and execution of bilateral lease deed on 8.4.93 and as such the appeal is liable to be dismissed. 

 7. Plaintiff's prayer for stay of further proceedings, out of which this appeal has arisen, and the fate of the suit itself depend upon the determination of only one main issue, namely, whether the Jalmahal in question is located within the alleged Chingri Gher of the plaintiff so as to attract the above circular. The learned Subordinate Judge has noticed in his order dated 4.4.93 that there are two conflicting reports on the above issue, one by the Assistant Commissioner (Land) dated 13. 12. 92 which is in favour of the Plaintiff and the other by the Thana Nirbahi Officer dated 29.12.92 which is against him and as such he has found it difficult to hold that the disputed Jalmahal is an integral part of the 'Chingri Gher'. In the circumstances of the case, we consider it right and proper that the issue as above and the suit itself should be finally decided upon taking evidence maintaining the status quo and this should be done as quickly as possible. Respondent No. 5 in his concise statement rightly stated that the alleged 'Chingri Gher' is a question of fact determinable in the trial upon taking evidence. Whatever evidence the parties may choose to lead, a quick local investigation may be helpful to decide the matter. The learned Subordinate Judge is directed to dispose of the suit with utmost expedition keeping in view that the order of status quo, which we are going to extend, will give the Plaintiff-appellant an extra advantage, as he is in possession of the Jalmahal without being granted lease for 1400 B.S and without payment of rent for this year and cause prejudice to Respondent No. 5 for each passing day as he has been granted lease and rent has also been paid. Parties be directed to take steps quickly and adjournment, if at all, should be granted for shortest possible time and only on compulsive grounds.
